the new compensators are (a) open loop stable, (b ) require much smaller values of controller gain than the conventional controllers, and above all (b) guarantee closed loop stability and loop-transfer recovery.

(a) a new compensator design for exact LTR is proposed, (b) the proposed compensator structure is open-loop stable and guarantees closed-loop stability, (c) the proposed compensatory design requires much smaller values than the conventional observer controller for exact LTR and above all (d) the new compensator design has the potential to solve many practical control problems such as reduction in controller bandwidth and control saturation problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a stable observer based controller for LTR.
the design and analysis of a new compensator for the loop transfer recovery problem.
the design of controllers which guarantee closed-loop stability and at the same time provide a high degree of loop transfer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new compensators are (a) much simpler, (b) require smaller values of gain and (c) are more robust to control saturation than the conventional observer-based controllers for the same degree loop transfer recovery.
the proposed compensator design provides a very simple and elegant solution to the problem of loop transfer recovery.

the new compensators proposed in this paper are much better suited to practical applications than conventional LTR controllers, especially in situations where the control signal is subject to saturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been successful in understanding the loop transfer recovery phenomenon and in designing a controller which is open-loop stable and which requires much smaller values (in fact, 1/10th of the conventional controller) of gain than the existing compensator for loop transfer recovery.
the proposed new compensator design for LTR is (i) a new compensator design, (ii) is open-loop stable, and (iii) requires much smaller gains than conventional observer based controllers.
the conventional controller structure for LTR is not a very efficient one and the new compensator is much more efficient than the conventional compensator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conventional compensator structure for exact and approximate loop-transfer recovery can be replaced by a new compensator that requires much smaller values for gain and has a simpler structure.
